splitSections.heading: How Do Dubai Patients Choose a Clinic?
splitSections.body: Dubai's patients come from many countries and carry different insurance plans. Both shape how they search and which clinic they choose.

points.title: Insurance first
points.body: Many patients check whether a clinic accepts their insurance network before comparing doctors or locations.

points.title: Many languages

points.title: Licence and credentials

points.title: Area and access
points.body: Parking, metro access and the drive from home or office influence the final choice.

faqs.q: How do you choose the best digital marketing company in Dubai for a clinic?
faqs.a: Do thorough research. Look at client testimonials, a healthcare portfolio and a track record you can verify. Then test its DHA knowledge: the company should know the banned words, title rules and medical director approval process. Ask whether it reports patient visits or stops at leads.

faqs.q: What DHA rules apply to clinic ads on social media?
faqs.a: DHA standards cover posts and ads on platforms such as Instagram, Facebook, TikTok and WhatsApp. They ban words like "the best" and "100 per cent", require titles to match the DHA licence, and need medical director approval for every post naming a facility.

faqs.q: Can Dubai clinics use patient testimonials and before-and-after photos?
faqs.a: Yes, with conditions. DHA rules require written patient consent, plus separate parental consent for under-18s. Before-and-after photos must show the same person, use the same lens, have no editing and carry a disclaimer that results vary. India's rules are stricter and ban both.

faqs.q: Do these rules apply to clinics in Dubai Healthcare City?
faqs.a: Not in the same way. Facilities in Dubai Healthcare City and DIFC fall under their own regulators rather than the DHA. Their advertising rules differ, so campaigns for these clinics are checked against the framework that applies to their licence.

faqs.q: Should Dubai clinic ads be in Arabic, English or other languages?
faqs.a: Match the languages your patients actually use. English and Arabic cover the base, while Hindi, Malayalam, Urdu or Tagalog ads may suit clinics serving those communities. Run versions side by side and compare patient visits by language, with DHA wording rules applied in each.
